input:
The lower figure, however, leaves the upgrade project exposed in a way that the headline saving does not immediately reveal. The float has been set at 6% because the work it protects is not a single activity but a chain: each stage of the upgrade proceeds from the finish of the one before it, and a delay in an early stage is inherited by every later stage unless float stands in front of it. Adverse weather stops outdoor work without regard for the programme. Deliveries arrive late for reasons outside the project's control. Tie-ins to the operating plant wait for shutdown windows set by the plant, not by the project. A smaller float absorbs none of this; it simply transfers the overrun into the completion date, where it costs more.

The steering group asked whether the float could be reduced and the saving taken now. The saving is real but small against the cost of a late finish, and it is taken once, while the exposure runs for the whole construction period. The figures themselves are set out in the Costs section and are not repeated here. The float is accordingly held at 6% until the long-lead items are on site, and the case for releasing part of it is made again then, against the work actually remaining
